samples.question: This picture shows a one-way lane network. Every disc is a junction and every straight gray bar is a lane joining the two junctions at its ends. Each lane carries exactly one black arrowhead at its middle, and that arrowhead points along the only direction in which that lane may be travelled. You start at the green junction. You may move only along lanes, and on each lane only the way its arrowhead points; you may pass through any number of junctions on the way and you may never move against an arrowhead. Three junctions are colored tanks: one blue, one orange and one purple; all other junctions are gray. Lanes join all of these junctions when the arrowheads are ignored, so how near a tank sits to the green junction on the page, how many lanes touch it, and where it lies do not matter; only travel that follows the arrowheads counts. Exactly one of the three tanks can be reached from the green junction under this rule. Which colored tank can be reached from the green junction? Answer blue, orange, or purple.
